title: Exact R-192 production-slot search remains empty in the selected source index
question: Does the current selected claim-filtered legacy source index contain an admitted production record for the exact R-192 heat-root, filtration/replica, raw-current, and q-ledger slots?
method: Run the configured legacy_search query for the exact token heat_root_incidence with the A13 claim filter and limit 50.
Run the exact phrase query root filtration conditional replicas with the same claim filter and limit 50.
Run the exact phrase query raw current spatial intertwiner q ledger with the same claim filter and limit 50.
Treat zero rows as absence from the selected/indexed corpus only, not as a universal absence theorem.
finding: All three bounded exact-token searches returned zero rows: heat_root_incidence, root filtration conditional replicas, and raw current spatial intertwiner q ledger. No selected source record therefore discharges the R-192 first failure slot or its dependent owner fields. This strengthens the existing EXP-000980 bounded search and R-192/R-193 boundary without claiming that no unindexed or future source could supply the fields.
decision_reason: The exact source-slot contract is load-bearing. A finite F_ref or diagonal-Gaussian comparison cannot be promoted when the selected source index contains no record of the required production generator/root/filtration/current/q-ledger data. The correct action is to keep A13 and the progressive gate open and require a hash-pinned owner before rerunning R-192.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing bounded source-index audit only. It does not prove global source absence, refute a future production owner, close A13/T-050, establish an interacting measure, physical-empty ordering, OS/KMS or real-time dynamics, thermodynamic/continuum limits, Sector-A, or Pre-A.
next_action: Require a stable source or newly authorized production package that hash-pins the nonlinear A1 mobility, heat_root_incidence, root-labelled filtration and conditional replicas, raw-current spatial identity, and once-owned nonnegative q-ledger; then rerun the unchanged R-192 owner order.
